subject: Staggered credit allocations flagged — verify legitimacy before issuance
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Sep 2025 09:12:34 -0700
Subject: Staggered grant pattern: batch of ~420 signups from acme-retail.org

Marcus / Neha —

Fraud heuristics picked up a staggered issuance pattern tied to ~420 new signups over the last 6 hours that requested the self-serve promo grant. Key signals: same org domain (acme-retail.org) but slightly varying localparts (+1..+420), low entropy passwords, identical device fingerprint family (see attached sample), and repeated use of the same IP ranges with short gaps (~10–30s).

I attached a small CSV with the top 30 rows (signup_batch_sample.csv) and the raw device signals (device-signals-20250905.json). Looks like either an automated onboarding test hitting production grants or a scripted abuse.

Recommendation: hold further self-serve grant issuance for acme-retail.org pending quick verification. If we pause grants, we should be careful about impacting legitimate onboarding runs. Can we loop in the partner contact to confirm?

Thanks,
Priyom
Senior Growth Ops Analyst
Redwood Inference

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Sep 2025 10:02:11 -0700
Subject: Re: Staggered grant pattern: batch of ~420 signups from acme-retail.org

Thanks Priyom —

I pulled the routing logs. These accounts were auto-approved by the self-serve ruleset v1.9 (no manual review). Two quick notes:
- The promo-grant rule has a rate cap of 5 grants/min globally; however, we recently added a soft-exemption for verified partners which can allow bursts during partner-driven onboarding flows.
- The org is on our partner allowlist (ApiWise is their integration partner), but we do not currently require partner-confirmation for every grant.

I will reach out to the ApiWise contact and ask them to confirm whether the activity was an automated test. If they confirm, we can mark the burst as valid and backfill any revoked grants. If not, we should revoke the suspect grants and patch the rule to add a per-org cap.

Action items:
1) Pause self-serve promo grants for acme-retail.org (Prio: high) — Priyom, can your script do a quick rule disable for that domain?
2) Ask ApiWise to confirm test runs and provide any test-run logs — Monica, can you reach out?
3) If ApiWise confirms negative, open ABUSE-2319 and start revocation + credit rollback.

— Marcus
Director, Growth & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

---

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Signe Korsgaard <signe@apiwise.com>, onboarding@acme-retail.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Sep 2025 11:37:50 -0700
Subject: Quick verification: large set of self-serve grants linked to acme-retail.org

Hi Signe / ACME onboarding team —

We noticed a large, staggered set of trial credit grants that appear to originate from acme-retail.org. Because partners sometimes run automated onboarding tests, wanted to confirm whether ApiWise (or your internal QA) ran a bulk test earlier today.

Details: ~420 signups between 03:00–09:00 UTC, similar device fingerprints and IP clusters. We paused further self-serve grants for that domain as a precaution.

Can you confirm:
- Was this an intentional test or an automated QA run?
- If yes, can you provide the test-run log(s) or the pattern so we can whitelist the QAT bot properly? If not, please advise if we should proceed with revocation.

Attaching the CSV subset we observed for convenience.

Thanks — appreciate the quick triage.

Best,
Monica Patel
Partner Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: signup_batch_sample.csv

---

From: Signe Korsgaard <signe@apiwise.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, onboarding@acme-retail.com
Date: Fri, 5 Sep 2025 14:08:22 +0200
Subject: Re: Quick verification: large set of self-serve grants linked to acme-retail.org

Hi Monica / team —

Thanks for flagging. We ran an automated onboarding test this morning as part of a staged rollout for ACME Retail; the test harness spins up multiple ephemeral users to exercise the integration. I am attaching the ApiWise test-run log (apiwise-test-run-log.txt) which includes timestamps and the list of ephemeral emails used. The behavior lines up with what you observed — the localparts are predictable because the harness appends a numeric suffix.

Two requests on our side:
1) Because the test intentionally exercises the full flow, can you provide a temporary sandbox exemption so our QA bots do not trigger anti-abuse in the future? Ideally whitelist by the integration client ID rather than domain.
2) If you revoke the accidental grants, please let us know the mechanism so we can reconcile our test metrics.

Note: ACME onboarding@acme-retail.com confirms the run was intentional (see reply below).

Thanks,
Signe Korsgaard
Onboarding Lead, ApiWise

Attachment: apiwise-test-run-log.txt

---

Onboarding Team <onboarding@acme-retail.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Signe Korsgaard <signe@apiwise.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Sep 2025 14:14:01 +0200
Subject: Re: Quick verification: large set of self-serve grants linked to acme-retail.org

Confirmed — that was a scheduled rollout QA run across multiple regions. No fraudulent intent. We ran the test to validate our provisioning scripts. Sorry for the disruption; we'll coordinate future runs with Redwood ahead of time.

--
ACME Retail Onboarding

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Sep 2025 08:45:09 -0700
Subject: Re: Staggered grant pattern: batch of ~420 signups from acme-retail.org

Thanks for the quick verification chain. Given the confirmation and the ApiWise test-run logs, recommended path:
1) Roll back the temporary pause immediately and re-enable self-serve grants for acme-retail.org.
2) Create a scoped exemption for the ApiWise integration client ID (not the entire domain) so partner QA runs can be identified. Priyom: can you add an allowlist by partner-client-id and limit to 1k/day?
3) Add a short-term monitoring alert (ABUSE-2319) to notify Growth and Security if a similar burst hits a different org or if the same pattern repeats without a partner confirmation.

I will coordinate with Security to ensure the exemption is logged and auditable.

Neha
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Sep 2025 16:02:11 -0700
Subject: Re: Staggered grant pattern: batch of ~420 signups from acme-retail.org

All — closing the loop: I restored self-serve promo grants for acme-retail.org at 15:30 UTC after ApiWise confirmed the test. Priyom implemented a partner-client-id based exemption and capped it to 1,000 grants/day; change is documented in ABUSE-2319 and linked to HubSpot ACME account.

Follow-ups:
- Monica: please confirm with ApiWise we will notify in advance for future large runs and provide the client-id allowlist instructions (copy the DocuSign link).
- Neha: can you and Security confirm the exemption is auditable by midnight PST?

Thanks everyone for the fast turnaround.

— Marcus
Director, Growth & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
